Genetic Variation
Polymorphisms (variations) exist within genes throughout 
the population.17 Most of these variations are not a cause for
concern. Th e outcome of a given variation depends on its na-
ture and location within a given gene. In other words, a speciﬁ c
variation may have no appreciable eﬀ ect on the production and
function of the protein product. However, it is also possible that 
a single nucleotide change or a more complex alteration in a
single gene can have profound eﬀ ects.
Inheritance Inheritance of speciﬁ c genes can be classi-
ﬁ ed as autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, X-linked 
dominant, X-linked recessive, or Y-linked.18 Because individ-
uals inherit one copy of each gene from each of their parents,
